newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Burg gets death threat over Swiss funds.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Burg gets death threat over Swiss funds.

text.p: A death threat has been sent from Switzerland to Avraham Burg, the leader of a Jewish group campaigning to investigate Swiss bank accounts left by Jews killed in the Holocaust, his office said on Thursday.

Burg is the chairman of the Jewish Agency, which together with other Jewish groups, has demanded compensation for the heirs of Jews who hid their money in Swiss banks in World War Two and were then murdered by the Nazis.

The threat, forwarded to Reuters, consisted of the words "Dead Soon" scrawled in English on a photocopy of a French-language article about Burg's demand a former Swiss president apologise for calling the Jewish inquiries "blackmail".
A picture of Burg accompanying the article was crossed out with an "x" and his eyes were blacked out.

A longer message typed onto the same page in French reads: "Don't ever come to Switzerland or the area, you are a dead man. We are tired of hearing bastards like you. Switzerland doesn't need preaching from people like you."
Police was not available for immediate comment but the Jewish Agency said it was not the first such threat Burg has received in recent weeks.

Swiss Economy Minister Jean Pascal Delamuraz, speaking before ending his term as president last month, described Jewish demands for a $250 million dollar fund to compensate families of Holocaust victims as "extortion and blackmail".

A commission including Swiss and U.S. bankers as well as Jewish representatives is investigating the scope of Holocaust accounts in Swiss banks. Six million Jews were systematically killed in the Holocaust under Adolf Hitler's Nazi Germany during World War Two.
